t: This is Piccadilly, just under a mile of road running between Hyde Park Corner and Piccadilly Circus, south of Mayfair. It's one of the widest and straightest streets in central London. Several notable people were born or died along it. Field Marshal Sir George Pollock, who relieved the garrison at Jalalabad in 1842, was born here. So was the dramatist James Planché. Antarctic explorer Apsley Cherry-Garrard, who wrote The Worst Journey in the World, died here. Princess Margaret once lived on this road.
